arc: One scene carrying the whole announcement as a single continuous camera move across one drawing: hook (the title BRANDS under a hatched arc) → feature (the kit of parts: colours, mark, typeface, references) → reveal (the peak, three scene frames taking the brand in turn under "EVERY SCENE on brand") → workflow (a cursor clicks the brand chip in a composer) → cta (the mark and "DOWNLOAD GENMOTION").

scenes.title: A feature announcement drawn as one engineering blueprint, the camera panning across five stations of a single sheet
scenes.summary: 16s, and the whole video. Paper white sheet, dark ink linework, a tick ruler along the bottom and a running header ("05 WHAT'S NEW" left, "GENMOTION · BRANDS" right) that tracks the camera so it stays pinned. Five stations are laid out left to right along about 6,600px of world. A: a hatched arc sweeping up to a boxed title "BRANDS" with "now built into genmotion" beneath it, part numbers BR-1180 and BR-0421 called out on the arc, and a slashed circle tagged "NEW". B: "YOUR BRAND, ONCE" over a kit of parts, two filled swatches ringed in ink labelled "#C6F91E  #16F5BD", the pinwheel mark in its own ring, a type specimen "Aa" in a box under "TYPEFACE", and three stacked reference cards under "ASSETS". C: the peak, a large circle with a chord and engraving hatch below it, titled "EVERY SCENE / on brand", holding three small scene frames that fill one after another with the lime hex, the mark and the typeface, labelled HEX, MARK, TYPE; a slashed circle tagged "ATTACH" arrows into it. D: "PICK IT IN THE COMPOSER", a composer box with the placeholder "describe your video…", and a brand chip that a cursor travels to, presses, and which then fills with ink and reads "GENMOTION" beside the mark, with a click ring expanding out of it. E: the mark inside a ticked ring, "DOWNLOAD GENMOTION" and "genmotion.dev". An ink line wipes the sheet clean over the last 14 frames.
scenes.build: Two components carry it. `components/drawing.ts` is a blueprint toolkit: a PALETTE, a `Strokes` class that batches many line segments into one geometry and reveals them by a 0 to 1 progress (so a whole arc, a circle or a field of hatching draws itself from one `.set()` call), a `Label` that renders text into a canvas texture with optional box and fill, and generators for `line`, `poly`, `arcPts`, `circle`, `rect`, `dashed` and `arrow`. `components/mark.ts` builds the GenMotion pinwheel as real geometry rather than an image. The scene itself is an orthographic camera over a single static world group: nothing in the drawing moves, the camera does. `camX` is the sum of three eased `interpolate` pans plus `f * 0.35`, a slow constant drift, so the frame never fully parks between stations, and the header group is set to the same x every frame so it reads as fixed furniture. Everything else is a `prog(frame, start, duration)` helper feeding `.set()` on strokes and labels, which makes the whole 495 frame timeline a readable column of start times. The peak is three `scale.x` reveals 12 frames apart; the cursor is a `THREE.Shape` whose tip is the group origin, lerped along an arc to the chip, scaled down on the press and eased away afterwards.
scenes.reuse: Take this when an announcement or explainer should feel considered and technical rather than glossy: a changelog film, an API or infrastructure feature, a hardware spec, a methodology explainer, anything where a diagram is the honest way to say it. The reusable ideas are the long-sheet camera pan (one static world, a moving orthographic camera, pans summed with a constant drift), the progress-driven `Strokes` batch that lets any amount of linework draw itself from one number, and the call-out grammar of slashed circles, leader lines and dashed construction between stations. Swap the station contents, the x constants and the pan keyframes. Do not copy the GenMotion pinwheel in `mark.ts` or the lime and teal swatches: those are GenMotion's own identity, and a brand video should carry the brand it is for.
